title: A benchmark suite under benchmarks/ times create and search as whole processes
body:
There is no benchmark in the repository. The timing scripts live under `tmp-claude/2026-11-02-refactor-survey/`, untracked: `construct/bench.sh` times three `create` kinds with two binaries interleaved, and `step4/gen.py` writes a 50 MB synthetic FASTA. The fixtures under `data/` are under 600 KB.

## Proposal

A separate cargo project at `benchmarks/`, with its own `[workspace]` so it stays out of the crates' build, clippy and test. Every measurement is one `sufr` process timed with `wait4`, so wall, user and system time and peak RSS come from one call.

- Two 1 GiB fixtures generated once into `benchmarks/runs/` from a fixed seed: DNA records with Alu-sized repeats, and protein records with log-normal lengths. A query file of 1,000,000 20-mers cut from the DNA.
- `create` rows: `--dna --write-lcp`, `--dna -m 20`, `--dna -s MASK`, and the protein file with no flags. Each runs cold and warm, so the run itself shows what the page cache costs.
- `count`, `locate` and `extract` rows over the query file, each in memory, with `-l` and with `-v`, cold.
- `--bin label=path`, repeatable. The default builds this tree. Rows for several binaries are interleaved and the order flips each repeat. A dry run of each row hashes its output, and the run fails when two binaries disagree.
- `--threads` is required and sets both `-t` and `RAYON_NUM_THREADS`. Each row reports CPU as (user + sys) / wall, so a run that uses more cores than asked is visible.
- The board from sail's benchmarks, with its `michi` sink replaced by two plain methods. Median and min wall, peak RSS, CPU, and a ratio against the first row of each group. One TSV row per measurement beside the board, so two runs can be joined later.

## Rejected

- Peer tools (libdivsufsort, libsais, CaPS-SA). Jack decided against them.
- A workspace member. A member cannot set its own profile, and its dependencies would ride every workspace build.
- `michi` as the pipeline. The run loop is a plain loop over bins and repeats, and `wait4` is one libc call.
